children: US natural gas flows to LNG export plants fell on Tuesday to about 19.2 billion cubic feet per day from 19.5 bcfd the previous day, as feedgas deliveries to Cheniere Energy's
Sabine Pass facility in Louisiana dropped sharply, according to preliminary data from financial firm LSEG.
• Feedgas to Sabine Pass, the largest liquefied natural gas export plant in the US, declined to about 4.2 bcfd on Tuesday from more than 5.0 bcfd the previous day.
• The drop suggests at least one liquefaction train at the facility may have been offline or may be operating at reduced rates.
• Feedgas deliveries to Freeport LNG, the fourth-largest US LNG export facility, remained at about 1.5 bcfd on Tuesday, lower than its usual 2 bcfd, according to LSEG data.
• Cheniere declined to comment; Freeport LNG did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
• The US is the world's largest LNG exporter and has become an increasingly important supplier to global markets since the outbreak of the Iran war.
• Traders watch LNG feedgas levels for an early indication of export activity and demand for US natural gas.
